title: Verifier‑Assisted versus LLM‑Only Pre‑deployment Network‑Change Validation: A Preregistered Paired Study
abstract: We measured whether adding a deterministic pre‑deployment verifier plus a bounded automated repair step increases the fraction of intent‑driven network‑change proposals that pass semantic validation relative to accepting a single LLM candidate. In a preregistered paired design (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001) we ran 300 paired intents stratified by difficulty (100 each: low/medium/high) using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5. The shared_initial protocol reused one LLM candidate per intent for both conditions to isolate deterministic rescue from resampling benefits. Results: baseline 299/300 unflagged passes (0.9966667), guarded 300/300 (1.0); contingency n11=299, n10=1, n01=0, n00=0; absolute paired difference = 0.0033333; exact two‑sided McNemar p = 1.0; paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI = [0.00,0.01] (bootstrap_seed = 1729, B = 10000). Under the supplied synthetic suite and a one‑repair budget the generator was near ceiling, limiting observable deterministic rescue. We release the preregistration and execution artifacts and interpret these findings with respect to estimand conditioning, validator coverage, repair budget, and operational tradeoffs.

sections.introduction:
Generative large language models (LLMs) are increasingly proposed for NetOps tasks such as intent→configuration translation, template synthesis, and automated repair. For pre‑deployment network changes, semantic correctness (sequencing, reachability, policy preservation) is operationally critical; superficial syntactic checks are insufficient. A common architecture pairs generation with deterministic validators and bounded automated repair (generate→validate→repair) to reduce deployment risk. However, measurable benefit from such guarded pipelines depends on what is held fixed (the estimand), the single‑shot quality of the generator, the validator's semantic reach, and the permitted repair budget.

This study tests a narrowly specified, operationally meaningful question: when a system policy limits model calls so that only one LLM draw is available per proposed change, does adding a deterministic verifier plus at most one automated repair increase the probability that that identical candidate will pass semantic pre‑deployment validation compared with accepting it without repair? We operationalize this by a preregistered paired design that reuses a single shared_initial LLM candidate per intent and compares (a) baseline — accept single candidate, and (b) guarded — deterministic validation plus ≤1 constrained repair. Contributions: (1) a preregistered paired evaluation isolating deterministic rescue under the shared_initial estimand; (2) an artifact‑archived execution and analysis bundle documenting validator traces and the solitary repair; and (3) an evidence‑grounded discussion of ceiling effects, estimand selection, and operational implications for NetOps CI/CD policies.
sections.related_work:
Recent surveys and system papers document rapid application of LLMs to network management tasks and stress the need for semantic evaluation beyond syntactic correctness [1],[2]. Tool‑augmented agentic frameworks (planner‑centric and ReAct‑style) enable LLMs to call external validators and simulators and are actively proposed for NetOps workflows [3],[4]. Empirical reports show generate→validate→repair scaffolds can improve surface correctness metrics relative to unconstrained generation, but reported gains depend strongly on validator coverage, task distributions, and whether pipelines permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration [4],[5].

Two methodological themes motivate our design. First, many prior evaluations conflate deterministic validator benefits with gains from additional model draws or iterative regeneration; isolating the single‑draw deterministic rescue requires conditioning on a shared LLM output [4],[6]. Second, NetOps evaluation suites often emphasize template or syntactic correctness rather than semantic invariants (reachability, sequencing, policy preservation), limiting operational generality [7]. Work combining symbolic verification and generative repair reports promising but variable success dependent on fault classes and verifier expressiveness [8]. Our experiment situates itself within these threads by fixing a single LLM draw and a bounded repair budget to measure the deterministic rescue that is possible under strict model‑call policies.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and estimand. The confirmatory protocol and analysis plan were preregistered (study id cnsmp2026-llm-verifier-predeployment-001; preregistration SHA‑256 = 425cb1652354120cf48f686b964723d64c76d0a8abe53cd5b5ad0eaa1af71fc7). The primary estimand is the absolute paired difference in the unflagged verifier‑pass proportion (guarded − baseline) computed on N = 300 paired intents following preregistered inclusion/exclusion rules. The confirmatory executor paired_binary_analysis_v1 and multiplicity plan were fixed before observing main‑run outcomes.

Task suite, stratification, and shared_initial protocol. Tasks were deterministically generated into a synthetic_topology_suite and stratified into low/medium/high difficulty (100 pairs per stratum) by explicit metadata (changed_interface_count, dependency_rule_count, required_command_count). To isolate deterministic validator/repair effects from resampling benefits, each pair used exactly one shared_initial candidate produced by the declared generator (gpt-5-mini) which was reused for both baseline and guarded conditions.

Validator, scoring rule, and repair operator. Semantic evaluation used deterministic_netops_validator_v5 applying the preregistered full_intent_constraint_validation rule. The validator deterministically checks sequencing invariants (e.g., must_be_down_for_fields), required command counts, preservation of unspecified state, topology reachability as encoded by the synthetic suite, and forbidden‑template protections. Scoring is binary: unflagged = pass. The guarded pipeline permitted at most one automated repair per flagged candidate; the repair operator was a constrained, localized edit routine limited to sequencing insertions and small local edits. Repairs were applied only when the validator deterministically flagged the shared_initial candidate and were re‑validated deterministically.

Execution, instrumentation, and pilot note. The run used the hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter under scientific_confirmatory mode. Planned_episode_count = 600 (300 pairs × 2 conditions); completed_episode_count = 600; complete_pair_count = 300; model_calls_used = 301 (300 shared_initial generations + 1 repair). The preregistration described an optional calibration pilot (n = 60) to estimate discordance and calibrate power; that pilot was not executed and no post‑preregistration power recalculation was performed. Exclusion rules specified pair exclusion only if both condition calls failed due to provider outages; no such dual‑call outages occurred.

Inferential procedures and CI choice. The preregistered primary test is an exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts (n10,n01) with an absolute paired difference estimate and a paired bootstrap percentile 95% confidence interval. We used a paired bootstrap (seed = 1729, B = 10000) to produce a CI for the absolute paired difference because the null distribution of the paired difference under minimal discordance is not well approximated by large‑sample normal approximations; the bootstrap supplies a distributional bound consistent with the paired design while acknowledging the low number of discordant pairs. Sensitivity analyses preplanned in the preregistration (failure‑as‑zero handling, stratum‑wise tests under multiplicity control, contamination checks) were retained as exploratory diagnostics and archived.
sections.results:
Execution integrity. The adapter completed the confirmatory run with completed_episode_count = 600 and complete_pair_count = 300. Provider/audit records show hosted_model_call_event_count = 301 and stage_counts indicating shared_initial_generation = 300 and repair = 1. Deterministic reconciliation confirmed consistent episode accounting and no excluded pairs.

Primary confirmatory outcomes. Binary scoring produced baseline_success_count = 299 and guarded_success_count = 300 (baseline = 299/300 = 0.9966667, guarded = 300/300 = 1.0). Contingency counts: n11 = 299, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. The exact two‑sided McNemar test on discordant counts returned p = 1.0. The observed absolute paired improvement (guarded − baseline) = 0.0033333. The paired bootstrap percentile 95% CI (seed = 1729, B = 10000) is [0.00,0.01]. The small number of discordant pairs (m = n10 + n01 = 1) limits sensitivity of exact inference; the bootstrap CI bounds the absolute paired improvement to at most one percentage point in this experimental context.

Per‑stratum diagnostics and repair trace. Per‑stratum tallies were: low baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; medium baseline = 100/100 and guarded = 100/100; high baseline = 99/100 and guarded = 100/100. The single discordant episode occurred in the high stratum and invoked the permitted automated repair. Validator traces attribute the initial failure to a sequencing omission (the required 'admin down' step was missing before a VLAN/MTU change). The constrained repair performed a single localized insertion of the missing sequencing command; after repair the deterministic validator returned valid == true. That repair is the solitary deterministic rescue recorded; all per‑episode validator traces and the repair transcript are archived with the run bundle for forensic inspection.

Operational cost. The guarded pipeline required only one additional repair stage call over 300 pairs (model_calls_used = 301), indicating minimal extra model‑call cost for the single observed rescue under the chosen repair design and synthetic suite.
sections.discussion:
Estimand conditioning and operational interpretation. The shared_initial estimand directly models policies that limit model calls per change request (cost, latency, governance). Under that policy the guarded pipeline measures only deterministic validator and bounded repair rescue applied to the identical candidate. Workflows that permit resampling or verifier‑guided regeneration change the estimand and typically increase success rates by exploiting generator variance; such regimes require separate preregistered evaluation.

Ceiling effects and pilot omission. Baseline single‑shot generation was near ceiling (299/300) on the chosen synthetic suite, producing minimal discordance (m = 1) and limited power to detect small absolute improvements. The omitted calibration pilot (n = 60) was intended to estimate discordance and inform sample sizing; not running it reduced the study's ability to anticipate ceiling performance and to predefine a detectable minimal effect under observed generator quality.

Validator coverage and failure‑mode dependence. The lone failure was a sequencing omission; reachability, ACL semantics, or other failure classes were rare in this synthetic distribution. The guarded pipeline's marginal value therefore depends on (a) deployed failure‑mode frequencies and (b) validator expressiveness: richer validators detecting reachability or policy semantics could increase observed rescue rates. Conversely, operator policies that disallow automated edits constrain guarded pipelines to detection and human escalation.

Repair budget and tradeoffs. We intentionally bounded repair to one constrained edit to measure minimal deterministic rescue under strict model‑call budgets. Allowing iterative repairs, larger edit operators, or interactive verifier‑guided generation would create other estimands and likely increase rescues but at higher model‑call and governance cost. The observed repair_stage_count = 1 quantifies the low marginal model‑call cost for the single rescue in this run.

Implications for NetOps CI/CD. Organizations should align evaluation estimands with operational policies: if multiple model calls are permitted, evaluations should allow resampling and interactive steering; if calls are tightly budgeted, the shared_initial estimand provides an operationally meaningful bound for deterministic verifier/repair rescue applied to a single candidate. Our archival artifacts enable practitioners to replay episodes and to assess how alternative repair operators or validator enrichments would alter rescue rates.
sections.conclusion: In a preregistered, artifact‑archived paired experiment using gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 on 300 synthetic NetOps intents, baseline single‑shot generation produced 299/300 verifier‑unflagged proposals and the guarded (validator + ≤1 repair) pipeline 300/300. The absolute paired difference was 0.0033333 (exact McNemar two‑sided p = 1.0; paired bootstrap 95% CI [0.00,0.01], seed = 1729, B = 10000). The guarded pipeline produced a deterministic rescue for a single sequencing omission with one constrained edit. Because baseline performance was near ceiling under the shared_initial estimand and repair budget, observable deterministic benefit was correspondingly small. We release full preregistration, execution, and analysis artifacts to enable targeted follow‑ups that vary estimand conditioning, model strength, task distributions, or repair budgets to evaluate other operational regimes.

limitations: Synthetic benchmark: tasks and topologies were deterministically generated and may not capture the full heterogeneity of production networks; real‑world failure‑mode frequencies may differ.
Single model and validator: only gpt-5-mini and deterministic_netops_validator_v5 were evaluated; results may not generalize to other LLMs or to richer/diverse validators.

Ceiling effect: baseline single‑shot performance was near 100% on this suite (299/300), producing minimal discordance and reduced sensitivity to small absolute improvements relative to larger prespecified targets.
Pilot omitted: the preregistered calibration pilot for discordance estimation was not executed, which reduced prior knowledge about achievable discordance and limited power anticipation.

Estimand conditioning: the shared_initial protocol conditions the estimand on a single LLM draw and therefore does not capture verifier benefit achievable through resampling or interactive regeneration.
Repair budget: the guarded condition allowed at most one constrained automated repair per pair; iterative or more permissive repair strategies may yield different results.
